@luau/global/class.documentation: Reflection over Luwu classes and the objects built from them.

@luau/global/class.fields.documentation: Returns a table of the public instance fields of a class or object, and whether that table is complete. Given an object, each field maps to that object's value for it; given a class, every field maps to none, since there is no instance to read values from. private fields are always skipped, and their absence is what makes the second return false.

@luau/global/class.fields/param/0.documentation: A class, or an object of one. Anything else raises an error.

@luau/global/class.fields/return/0.documentation: The public instance fields, keyed by name.

@luau/global/class.fields/return/1.documentation: true when every field of the class is present, false when one or more private fields were left out.

@luau/global/class.isinstance.documentation: Returns true if o is an object of the class c. This is exact class identity: an object built from a different class is never an instance of c, and a non-object value is never an instance of anything.

@luau/global/class.isinstance/param/0.documentation: The value to test. Any value is accepted; anything that isn't an object returns false.

@luau/global/class.isinstance/param/1.documentation: The class to test against. Must be a class, not an object of one.

@luau/global/class.isinstance/return/0.documentation: Whether o is an object of exactly the class c.

@luau/global/class.name.documentation:
Returns the name of a class, or of the class an object was built from.

Raises an error when given anything that is neither a class nor an object.

@luau/global/class.name/param/0.documentation: A class, or an object of one.

@luau/global/class.of.documentation: Returns the class an object was built from, or nil when o is not an object.

@luau/global/class.of/param/0.documentation: The value to inspect. Any value is accepted.

@luau/global/class.of/return/0.documentation: The object's class, or nil if o is not an object.

@luau/global/require.code_sample:
local sibling = require("./sibling")
local uncle = require("../uncle")
local fs = require("@std/fs")
@luau/global/require.documentation:
Loads the module at `path` and returns what it returned, running it the first time it is required and reusing that result afterwards.

A path is a string: `"./sibling"` and `"../uncle"` are relative to the requiring file, and an alias such as `"@std/fs"` resolves through the `aliases` of the nearest `.luaurc`.

@luau/global/require/param/0.documentation: Path of the module to load, relative to this file (`./`, `../`) or through a `.luaurc` alias (`@name/...`).

@luau/global/typeof.code_sample:
local result = pcall(risky)
if typeof(result) == "error" then
    -- result is narrowed to the `error` extern type here
    print(tostring(result))
end

if typeof(value) == "DateTime" then
    print(value:display())
end
@luau/global/typeof.documentation:
Returns the name of `value`'s type as a string.

On primitives it matches `type`, so `"nil"`, `"number"`, `"string"`, `"table"` and the rest come back as you'd expect.

Userdata is where it differs: an extern type reports its own name rather than `"userdata"`, so comparing against that name both tells you what you have and narrows the value to it.

@luau/global/typeof/param/0.documentation: The value to inspect. Any value is accepted, including `nil`.

@luau/global/typeof/return/0.documentation:
The name of the value's type.

It comes from the `__type` metafield if one is set. Only userdata can set it, which in practice means the extern types a host environment hands you. Tables can't rename themselves this way, and classes and objects always report `"class"` and `"object"`.
